newsitem.title: USA: Rhone-Poulenc p53 gene therapy shows action.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc p53 gene therapy shows action.

text.p: Houston researchers on Monday said the first gene therapy study of tumor suppressor p53 gene was safe and showed evidence of clinical activity, setting the stage for Phase II trials by Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.

Researchers from The University of Texas M.D. Anderson Cancer Center disclosed results of the Phase I trial of 30 patients with recurrent head and neck cancer during the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting being held here.

"The treatment appears to be safe and did not cause any serious side effects," researchers said in a prepared statement, adding it "resulted in tumor regression in several patients who could not undergo surgery for their recurrent tumors."
The dose-escalation trial is being sponsored by privately held Introgen Therapeutics Inc of Austin, Texas, and RPR Gencell, the gene therapy division of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer based in Collegeville, Pa.
All were end-stage patients who had failed conventional treatments, the researchers said, adding their tumors were directly injected with p53 gene that had been loaded into an adenovirus.

By the end of the trial five of the 17 non-operable patients were stable and two exhibited partial regression -- defined as at least a fifty percent reduction in injected tumor. They had received injections every other day for two weeks.
